To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the (GAA.TTC)n repeat is genetically unstable in E. coli and that genetic instability of the repeat is orientation-dependent, being greater when GAA is on the lagging strand.

RecA deficiency, RecBCD deficiency, and RecFOR deficiency all cause an increased rate of (GAA·TTCTTC)n instability, and that the instability is orientation dependent, i.e. the instability is greater when GAA is on the lagging strand.
the (GAA.TTC)n sequence is unstable when GAA serves the lagging strand and that this instability is due to inefficient processing of stalled replication.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the mechanisms of genetic instability of the expanded (GAA•TTC) n sequence, the most common mutation in the neurodegenerative disorder Friedreich ataxa.
the mechanism of genetic instability of the expanded (GAA ·TTC)n sequence in Friedreich ataxis and the role of RecA-dependent recombinations in this instability.
the genetic instability of the triplet repeat (GAA·GAA)n that is responsible for the most common form of Friedreich ataxa.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the (GAA.TTC)n sequence is more genetically unstable when GAA serves the role of the lagging strand.
the RecA-dependent RecBCD and RecFOR pathways are required for the maintenance of the (GAAA)n sequence.

the orientation-dependent genetic instability is due to a RecA-dependent mechanism that is likely to involve RecBCD and RecFOR pathways and is likely to be due to defective processing of stalled DNA replication forks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the genetic instability associated with Friedreich ataxa is caused by a defect in RecA-dependent recombiational restart of stalled DNA replication forks.
the (GAA•TTC)n sequence is genetically unstable because it is replication error-prone, and that the genetic instability is exacerbated by defective processing of stalled DNA replication forks.
RecA is required for the orientation-dependent instability and RecFOR and RecBDC are required for the orientation-independent instability of the (CAG)·(CTG)n sequence.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the (GAA•TTC)n sequence is genetically unstable when GAA serves the function of the lagging strand.
the orientation of a triplet repeat in a DNA molecule may have important biological consequences, and that triplet repeat instability may not be a random process.
RecA-dependent recombinations are required for the stability of the (GAATTC)n sequence when GAATTC is the lagging template strand.
